questions.q: A firm sells {q} units at £{p}. Its total costs are £{c}. What is its profit, in £?
Revenue is £{r}, costs excluding normal profit are £{c}, and normal profit is £{n}. What is abnormal profit, in £?

options: The average profit in the economy
The minimum profit needed to keep a firm in its current business
The profit a firm earns in a good year
questions.why: It covers the opportunity cost of the owner's resources.

questions.q: Economists treat normal profit as a cost of production.
questions.why: It is the return the firm must earn to keep operating.

questions.q: High profits in a market act as:
options: A signal that consumers want more, drawing in resources
A sign that resources should leave
A reason for firms to cut output

questions.q: Which is a role of retained profit?
options: It pays for investment without the need to borrow
questions.why: Profit kept in the business can fund new capital and research.

questions.q: Explain the role of profit in allocating resources in a market economy.

ideas.label: Profit is a signal or incentive showing what consumers want
Resources move towards profitable uses and away from loss-making ones

questions.model: Profit acts as a signal that consumers want more of something and gives an incentive to supply it. Resources move towards profitable uses and away from loss-making ones.
questions.why: Signal first, then the movement of resources.

tests.answer: High profit is a signal so new firms enter and resources move to that market.
Profit is an incentive for firms.
Profit is paid to the bank.
